h1: Magnetic sheet metal brakes — 2 to 10 ft, 16 gauge, boxes of any depth
intro: A magnetic sheet metal brake clamps the sheet with an electromagnet in the bed instead of a mechanical beam: a loose steel clamping bar is held down by 3.3 to 13.2 US tons of magnetic force, and because there is no beam frame at the ends, a short bar folds the side of a box of any depth, closed shapes, narrow channels and short return flanges that a box and pan brake cannot reach. NovoTech sells the EB range in Canada, all on this page: six models from the EB625 at 2 ft to the EB3200 at 10 ft, 16 ga mild steel over 2 to 8 ft and 18 ga over 10 ft, each with a set of clamping bars, a radius bar and a back stop, and the leaf angle read on a scale. Every model is in the table below with its length, clamping force and weight, then the family with its full specification and photos. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

groups.title: Magnetic sheet metal brakes
groups.lead: An electromagnet in the bed clamps the sheet under a steel bar — no beam frame at the ends, so a short bar folds the side of a box of any depth.

faq.q: What can a magnetic brake fold that a box and pan brake cannot?
faq.a: Anything the end frames of a conventional brake would block: the fourth side of a deep box, a closed or narrow channel, a short return flange, a flange inside a panel, a box with a lip. The clamping bars are loose pieces from 1″ long up, placed wherever the fold is, and the magnet holds whatever is under them. The price is capacity — 16 ga mild steel on the short models, 18 ga on the 10 ft — so for 14 ga and heavier the box and pan or hydraulic brakes are the machines.

faq.q: How strong is the clamping, and does the sheet slip?
faq.a: The EB brakes clamp with 3.3 to 13.2 US tons across the full length, two-stage: a light hold to position the sheet, full force to fold. The sheet does not slip in rated material; the clamping bar edge gives the bend radius, and a radius bar is supplied for larger radii. The magnet releases the instant the foot switch is let go.

faq.q: How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?
faq.a: In gauge of mild steel over the full length: 16 ga on the EB625 to EB2500 and 18 ga on the EB3200. Stainless steel bends at about two gauges lighter, aluminum at about two gauges heavier; shorter folds with a short clamping bar take heavier material than the full-length rating.

faq.q: What power does a magnetic brake need?
faq.a: Single-phase 120 or 240 V — a wall outlet: the electromagnet draws power only while the foot switch is pressed. No hydraulics, no three-phase, so the brake can go anywhere in the shop or on a trailer.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
